claims.content: Initiate Emergency Point Reports enables the System Operator to transmit a J3.1 message reporting an emergency point (the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts) and, through operator action only, to report on or assume reporting responsibility for a previously reported emergency point when additional or more current information is available.

goal.raw_text: Initiate Emergency Point Reports enables the System Operator to transmit a J3.1 message reporting an emergency point (the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts) and, through operator action only, to report on or assume reporting responsibility for a previously reported emergency point when additional or more current information is available.

claims.content: System Operator
An emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts exists.
If the emergency point has been previously reported, the System Operator has additional or more current information on the point.

If the System Operator is assuming R2 for an emergency point, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message has been received declaring the unit with R2 inactive, or no periodic update has been received for three consecutive update intervals.
The emergency point is not a reference point or space/ballistic missile track.

The System Operator initiates the use case by operator action when an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts exists and a J3.1 message reporting the emergency point is to be transmitted; or when the System Operator has additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point; or when the System Operator is assuming R2 for an emergency point because a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message has been received declaring the unit with R2 inactive, or no periodic update has been received for three consecutive update intervals.

trigger.raw_text: The System Operator initiates the use case by operator action when an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts exists and a J3.1 message reporting the emergency point is to be transmitted; or when the System Operator has additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point; or when the System Operator is assuming R2 for an emergency point because a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message has been received declaring the unit with R2 inactive, or no periodic update has been received for three consecutive update intervals.

claims.content: The System Operator transmits the emergency point as a J3.1 message used to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.

If the emergency point is related to a previously reported track/point, the System Operator includes the TN, Previously Reported as amplifying information in the J3.1 message and assigns a TN, Reference different from the TN, Previously Reported.

When IFF/SIF data are available, the System Operator transmits IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) in the J3.1 message, containing the IFF/SIF modes and codes of the previously reported track for which the emergency point was initiated.
When the System Operator has additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point, the System Operator reports on that point through operator action only.

If the System Operator is assuming R2 for an emergency point because a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message has been received declaring the unit with R2 inactive, or because no periodic update has been received for three consecutive update intervals, the System Operator uses the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
The latest JU to report a point has R2 for that point.
If the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 message, the report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.
If the emergency point is a reference point or space/ballistic missile track, the emergency shall not be initiated; exit use case.
If an alert is attempted for the J3.1 Emergency Point message, alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message since these points cannot be filtered; exit without setting the alert.

If the emergency point has an Activation Time in the future, i.e., Time Function = Activation Time and the Time has not yet arrived, the point shall not be reported as moving and Course and Speed shall be set to No Statement; exit the movement reporting path.
The emergency point has been reported as a J3.1 message used to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
The emergency point has been assigned a TN(s) by the reporting JU.

If the emergency point is related to a previously reported track/point, the J3.1 message contains, as amplifying information, the TN, Previously Reported associated with the emergency point, and the emergency point has a TN, Reference different from the TN, Previously Reported.

If IFF/SIF data are available, the J3.1 message contains IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes); in the case of an emergency point initiated for a previously reported track, those data contain the IFF/SIF modes and codes of that previously reported track.
If the System Operator assumed R2 for an emergency point, the System Operator used the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
The latest JU to report a point has R2 for that point.
If the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 message, the report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.
No emergency has been initiated on a reference point or space/ballistic missile track.
